{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Southwestern cuisine|Southwestern U.S. cuisine]]

These ribs use a Southwestern style rub, feature a sauce with a lot of prominent Mexican flavors, and are cooked over mesquite instead of hickory, which isn't very easy to find in the South, however mesquite is.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 slab St. Louis [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] ribs
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] light [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Habanero|habanero]] chile powder
* ¼ cup ancho [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder
* 1 tbsp dried Mexican [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tbsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Chipotle Pepper|chipotle]] powder
* 1 habanero chile, seeded and [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 ½ cups [[Cookbook:Kansas City Barbecue Sauce|barbecue sauce]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Tequila|tequila]] (recommended: José Cuervo Especial)
* Large mesquite chunks

== Procedure ==
#Combine sugar, chile powders, oregano, salt, and pepper. Remove membrane from ribs and rub both sides with mixture. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour to [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]].
#Combine tequila, habanero, and sauce. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium high heat. Set aside.
#Place enough mesquite chunks in a [[Cookbook:Smoker|smoker]] to keep the temperature at 200°F. Place ribs in smoker and cook 7 hours, [[Cookbook:Basting|basting]] every hour with sauce mixture.
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] meat side liberally with sauce mixture. Place sauce side-down on a high [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] and cook until well-browned. Brush other side with sauce and repeat 1 more time.
#Slice ribs into 1-rib portions and serve warm with remaining sauce.
